source: Human-authored databases curriculum; v2 revises prerequisite structure and concept abstraction. Not derived from Synapse gold JSONL or failure artifacts.
provenance: Human-authored databases curriculum; v2 revises prerequisite structure and concept abstraction. Not derived from Synapse gold JSONL or failure artifacts.
review_notes: v2 focuses on direct prerequisite semantics: fix inverted SQL chain, merge near-duplicate Relations, remove redundant Database Indexing overview, add Replication as a direct Distributed Databases prerequisite, and rewrite descriptions so selected concepts state what they presuppose.

change_log.old: db.sql requires db.joins (SQL overview above joins)
change_log.new: db.sql is foundational; db.select requires db.sql; db.joins requires db.select
change_log.reason: SQL is the language substrate for SELECT/joins, not a topic that presupposes joins
change_log.rationale: Treating SQL as leaf/overview after Joins inverted direct-prerequisite semantics and encouraged bidirectional SQL↔SELECT confusion.

change_log.new: removed; relational-table meaning covered by Relational Model + Tables (aliases retain 'Relations')
change_log.reason: Near-duplicate abstraction caused Tables↔Relations extras and unclear direction
change_log.rationale: At learning-unit scale, 'Relations' and 'Tables' were not distinct enough to justify separate nodes.

change_log.new: removed; responsibilities folded into Indexes + Query Planning
change_log.reason: Overview node forced a long chain Indexes→Query Planning→Database Indexing with weak directness
change_log.rationale: Database Indexing duplicated Indexes at a vaguer level and sat above Query Planning without adding a distinct learning unit.

change_log.reason: SELECT syntax is meaningless without the SQL language and table targets
change_log.rationale: Direct prerequisites for writing SELECT are table structure and SQL as the query language.

change_log.reason: Planning presupposes declarative queries as well as access paths
change_log.rationale: A query planner chooses plans for statements; Indexes alone omit the query side.

change_log.reason: Replication is a direct building block of distributed databases; consensus is a mechanism, not always a direct overview prerequisite
change_log.rationale: Understanding distributed databases directly requires replication and partitioning plus consistency trade-offs; consensus algorithms are advanced mechanisms under replication.

change_log.new: removed as hard prerequisite of the overview
change_log.reason: Consensus is not always a direct prerequisite of the distributed-database overview
change_log.rationale: Learners can grasp distributed DB design via replication/partitioning/consistency without first mastering consensus protocols; Consensus remains a selectable concept requiring Replication.

change_log.reason: Partition keys and shards presuppose tabular/relational data units
change_log.rationale: Partitioning is applied to stored relations/tables; Tables is a direct prerequisite.

change_log.reason: Replication copies stored data units; tables are the primary unit in this curriculum
change_log.rationale: Direct prerequisite: you replicate table/relation contents, so Tables comes first.

change_log.reason: After merging Relations, FDs attach to Tables; schema design also directly needs tables
change_log.rationale: Functional dependencies and schema design are about attributes of tables, not a separate Relations node.

change_log.new: descriptions name direct prerequisites in plain language
change_log.reason: Dependency generation only sees titles/descriptions, not inventory edges
change_log.rationale: Clearer prerequisite wording improves direct-edge generation without changing the dependency architecture.

concepts.title: Relational Model
concepts.description: Foundational data model: relations with tuples and attributes. No database-specific prerequisites; later concepts build on this model.

concepts.title: Tables
concepts.description: Named relations (tables) storing rows under a schema. Directly requires the Relational Model before treating tables as the unit of storage and design. Synonymous with relations-as-tables in this curriculum.

concepts.title: SQL
concepts.description: Declarative language for defining and querying relational data. Foundational language skill; SELECT and joins are expressed in SQL and therefore require it.

concepts.title: SELECT Queries
concepts.description: Retrieving and projecting rows with SQL SELECT. Directly requires Tables (what is queried) and SQL (the language of the statement).

concepts.title: Joins
concepts.description: Combining rows from multiple tables on related columns. Directly requires SELECT Queries; joins extend single-table retrieval rather than replacing SQL itself.

concepts.title: Disk Storage
concepts.description: How database pages and files are laid out on persistent storage. Foundational for index structures that sit on disk-oriented organization.

concepts.title: B-Trees
concepts.description: Balanced tree structures used for efficient equality and range lookups on disk-backed data. Directly requires Disk Storage.

concepts.title: Indexes
concepts.description: Auxiliary access paths that accelerate lookups and sorting. Directly requires B-Trees as the common physical structure for relational indexes.

concepts.title: Query Planning
concepts.description: Choosing an efficient execution plan for a declarative query. Directly requires SELECT Queries (the statements being planned) and Indexes (primary alternative access paths).

concepts.title: Replication
concepts.description: Copying table data across nodes for availability and locality. Directly requires Tables as the unit of replicated content.

concepts.title: Partitioning
concepts.description: Splitting table data across shards or partitions by a key. Directly requires Tables; partitioning is applied to relational data units.

concepts.title: Consensus
concepts.description: Agreeing on a single value or log among distributed nodes. Directly requires Replication; consensus is a coordination mechanism for replicated state.

concepts.title: Consistency Models
concepts.description: Guarantees about visibility and ordering of reads and writes across replicas. Directly requires Replication; models describe behavior of replicated data.

concepts.title: Distributed Databases
concepts.description: Databases spanning multiple nodes. Directly requires Replication, Partitioning, and Consistency Models as the core design axes; consensus protocols are related mechanisms under replication, not always a separate overview prerequisite.

concepts.title: Functional Dependencies
concepts.description: Constraints where attribute sets determine other attributes within a table. Directly requires Tables.

concepts.title: Normal Forms
concepts.description: Schema forms (1NF–BCNF etc.) defined via functional dependencies. Directly requires Functional Dependencies.

concepts.title: Normalization
concepts.description: Decomposing schemas according to normal forms to reduce redundancy. Directly requires Normal Forms.

concepts.title: Schema Design
concepts.description: Choosing tables, keys, and constraints for an application. Directly requires Normalization (design method) and Tables (the artifacts being designed).
